event.name: MRFA Research Day
event.intro:
MRFA Research Day is an annual scientific forum that showcases the outstanding research accomplishments of trainees, fellows, and associates across Mayo Clinic Florida. Through oral presentations, rapid-fire talks, and poster sessions, participants will share innovative discoveries, foster collaboration, and engage with faculty mentors and peers. The event celebrates research excellence while highlighting the impact of scholarly work on advancing science, improving patient care, and shaping the future of medicine.

The 2026 program features two sessions of oral and rapid-fire presentations, two poster sessions, and an awards ceremony recognizing outstanding scholarly contributions. Tap any talk to see the authors and send a question to the moderator.
event.fullName: Mayo Clinic Research Fellow’s Association (MRFA) Research Day, Florida 2026

award.title: How the Audience Choice Award works
text: In addition to the awards determined by the judging panel, MRFA Research Day recognizes one presentation with the Audience Choice Award, selected by the attendees in Kinne Auditorium.
After each talk, select “Rate this talk” in the program or scan the code below, choose the presentation, and rate it from one to five stars. Each talk becomes available for rating when it begins.

To keep the results fair, ratings require a Mayo Clinic sign-in, only one rating per attendee per presentation is counted, and ratings by a presentation’s own authors are excluded. Voting closes at 1:30 PM, and the recipient will be announced at the Awards Ceremony at 2:15 PM. Audience ratings are separate from the judges’ evaluations.

committee.sessions: Mayo Clinic Research Fellow’s Association - Florida - Chair
committee.bio: Regina Castaneda, MD, appointed as Florida Chair of the Mayo Clinic Research Fellow’s Association in 2026, is a postdoctoral research fellow in women’s health and internal medicine at Mayo Clinic Florida. Her research focuses on the intersection of obesity, menopause, and cardiometabolic health, with a particular interest in precision medicine approaches to obesity treatment in midlife women. She is currently pursuing a master’s degree in Clinical and Translational Sciences at the Mayo Clinic College of Medicine and Science. Dr. Castaneda has led multiple first-author publications in leading journals, including The Lancet, Annals of Internal Medicine, and JAMA Internal Medicine. She has been recently recognized with the 2026 Women in Endocrinology Young Investigator Award, the 2025 New Investigator Award from The Menopause Society, and the Excellence in Clinical Research Award from the Mayo Clinic Research Fellows’ Association. As an aspiring endocrinologist and physician-scientist, she is committed to advancing evidence-based care for women across the lifespan.

committee.name: Sebastian Fernandez-Bussy
committee.title: James C. and Sarah K. Kennedy Dean of Research, Mayo Clinic in Florida
committee.role: Professor of Medicine; Chair, Division of Pulmonary, Allergy and Sleep Medicine
committee.sessions: Dean of Research, Mayo Clinic Florida
committee.bio:
Sebastian Fernandez-Bussy, MD, the James C. and Sarah K. Kennedy Dean of Research at Mayo Clinic in Florida, serves as Professor of Medicine. He is an internationally recognized interventional pulmonologist and is Chair of the Division of Pulmonary, Allergy and Sleep Medicine and Director of both the Section of Interventional Pulmonology and the Procedure Innovation Team at Mayo Clinic Florida.

His clinical and research interests focus on advancing minimally invasive approaches to thoracic disease, including robot-assisted and translational bronchoscopy, bronchoscopic ablation for thoracic malignancies, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), central airway disorders, and the development of artificial intelligence–driven diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers. Dr. Fernandez-Bussy completed his medical training in Argentina and pursued advanced training at the University of Florida and Heidelberg University, where he currently serves as a Visiting Professor. In addition, he directs the Endoscopy Department of the Latin American Thoracic Society, contributing to the advancement of interventional pulmonology and pulmonary endoscopy worldwide.
